humanities_role_explanation: Items are general short-form factual questions drawn from many topics (science & technology, politics, art, geography, sports, music, TV, history); humanities topics supply some content but the competence tested is general factuality, not disciplinary skill.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only short questions with short text reference answers.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Short-form fact-seeking QA with a single indisputable answer (factual recall), answered in free text and graded correct/incorrect/not attempted. Calibration is measured through stated confidence and answer-frequency analyses ('know what they know').

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to one task: short-form factuality. Topics are diverse, but it is a single-format factual QA benchmark.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Claude-3-haiku, Claude-3-sonnet, Claude-3-opus, Claude-3.5-sonnet, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, o1-mini, o1-preview.

quantitative_metrics.note: Correct, not attempted, incorrect, correct given attempted, F-score, and calibration curves.

summary: SimpleQA is a 4,326-question benchmark of short, fact-seeking questions, adversarially collected against GPT-4 and each with a single, indisputable answer. Responses are graded as correct, incorrect or not attempted, and calibration is also analysed. Frontier models score below 50%.
key_findings: o1-preview scored highest (42.7% correct, F-score 44.8), then GPT-4o (38.2% correct). Claude models attempt fewer questions. All models overstate their confidence. o1-preview is the best calibrated. The authors estimate a benchmark error rate of about 3%.
facets_explanation: Reference answers were written by AI trainers (human annotators hired by the authors' organisation) with supporting web links. A second trainer independently answered each question and only agreeing items were kept. Ambiguous or multi-answer questions were removed or sent back for revision, and the 3% residual error is treated as a defect. The questions give no context, so answers need external knowledge. There is no per-community gold.
results_explanation: Table 3 reports o1-preview as the best model: 'OpenAI o1-preview 42.7 9.2 48.1 47.0 44.8', i.e. 42.7 correct and F-score 44.8; the headline value is the overall correct rate (accuracy). The paper evaluates a single question format. The third-trainer check (94.4%) is a data-quality figure, not a human baseline on the same metric.

humanities_role.quote: SimpleQA contains questions from a wide range of topics, including history, science & technology, art, geography, TV shows, etc.

dataset_size.quote: We present a benchmark called SimpleQA, which contains 4,326 short, fact-seeking questions.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: Please give your best guess, along with your confidence as a percentage that that is the correct answer

gold_source.quote: First, AI trainers (i.e., human annotators) created question and answer pairs.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: we asked AI trainers to create knowledge-seeking questions that fit a very specific set of criteria.

answer_multiplicity.quote: questions had to be written such that they only have a single, indisputable answer.

plurality_treatment.quote: we removed questions from the dataset if answers from two trainers didn’t agree according to a prompted ChatGPT classifier
